title: Research sprint goal: The open gaps of the endpoint, identity, security, arch, gitlab and logs articles are researched against the census
goal: The sprint goal's open questions are answered with the kb tools first and the live docs for the gaps, and the findings are written as kb facts and gap entries through the kb skills, so each committed item can name the knowledge it needs. Tested rows for kb/_self/_retrieval/lookup_eval.csv are a code-lane path (_tools/kblane.py): a story finished with them lands through backlog.py land ID --wait-merge SECONDS, not done --commit.
notes: 2026-10-20 planning: the sprint's items are research items themselves; this story only settles what they share before the first is claimed: the routes kb_pack gives for their topics after the census, and the live docs server each needs (microsoft-learn for the endpoint, identity and security topics; the web for arch, gitlab and logs). It waits for the census tag ST-ywqj4gva. 2026-10-21 findings. (1) Open gaps per sibling (no closing note, none dated 2026-10-21 or later): 68 security and privacy, 48 arch, 55 mecm, intune, autopilot, entra, graph, defender and auth, 47 gitlab and logs, 35 windows, dsc, ad and gpo: 253, none outside these groups. (2) Routes: kb_pack on a sampled gap question per group gave coverage good with the owning article and its UNK line (mecm/client-notification, logs/otel-python-sdk, gitlab/detecting-mr-merges-in-ci, arch/fluent-rust-typescript, entra/hybrid-deviceid-objectguid); one weak, a broad security question, still named security/secret-shapes-in-text. Read a gap's own article with rag.py show. (3) Live docs: microsoft-learn answers without login (endpoint, identity, security items use it first). For arch, gitlab and logs WebSearch needs allowed_domains (docs.gitlab.com, github.com, pypi.org, opentelemetry.io) and gives summaries: WebFetch the official page or pinned raw file for the fact. A sampled search found no page stating CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE for the default-branch pipeline after a merge. No outside facts: the questions were about this repository's pack routes, the ledger and which live servers answer here; no fact about an outside source was written.
